thread:
julia: Heads up — after the scrub/evict-change rollout we're seeing a sharp OOM spike on longctx hosts, started ~09:12 UTC. A bunch of pods restarted.
mark: saw it too, thanks for flagging. Is this the scrub patch that changed the fastpath drain heuristic?
julia: yes, the PR adjusted `evict_scrub_batch_size` and lowered the threshold for chunk coalescing. small change but wide rollout.
priya: putting logs and a short timeline: 09:08 deploy finished, 09:10 autoscaler ramped, 09:12 first OOMs, 09:14 80% of longctx cluster hit OOM.
dylan: can we repro locally? sequence length distribution might be the trigger (longtail).
mark: I ran a local soak with seqlen=4096 workload and hit memory pressure after ~3k requests. attaching a quick flame output:
mark: ```
Heap growth: kv_slab +70MB per 1k requests
Hot path: kv_prefetch -> slab_alloc -> kernel_router_lock
Backtrace: alloc_slab > prepare_eviction_scan > background_scrub
```
priya: interesting — flame shows background_scrub holding locks while slab_alloc runs, that could delay eviction and cause allocation backlog.
julia: CI perf didn't catch this — the unit tests use seqlen=1024 median, so the longtail path was untested.
ci-bot: Perf CI: no regressions flagged on default perf suite (seqlen 512/1024).
dylan: bisect plan: narrow down to the scrub/evict commits. I can run a binary-bisect across canary groups. @mark can you try a minimal reproducer with `--no-background-scrub`?
mark: yes i did: toggling `background_scrub=false` on the same build removes the OOMs in the soak. so scrub seems central.
priya: any kernel selection differences? We switched a kernel route in the rollout (kd-router v2) that changes allocation ordering. Could be a compounding factor.
julia: good point — the rollout included both scrub config and kernel-router flip in same CI group. we need to separate.
dylan: started a bisect: testing groups with kernel-router v1 + scrub v2 vs kernel-router v2 + scrub v1 etc. initial results: kernel-router v2 + scrub v2 -> OOM, kernel-router v1 + scrub v2 -> OOM but slower, kernel-router v2 + scrub v1 -> OK. suggests scrub v2 is main trigger but kernel v2 amplifies.
mark: extracted the reproducer command for others: `./soak --host longctx-1 --seqlen 4096 --concurrency 32 --requests 5000 --enable-prefetch`
priya: profiling snapshot (malloc counters) from an affected host: total_allocs up 2.7x, free_rate down 0.6x, avg_slab_fragmentation +12%.
julia: fragmentation jump is small but combined with delayed eviction caused net memory growth. I think scrub v2's `scan_window` was made too aggressive, it marks more pages but defers compaction.
dylan: suggestion: temporarily hold the scrub change and rollback only that part. kernel-router revert not needed immediately.
mark: I'm +1 on a targeted revert of the scrub heuristic. Could we hotfix by reducing `evict_scrub_batch_size` to previous value on config?
priya: yes we can push a config revert (no binary change) to canary region within 5m. I'll prepare the rollout: Revert config key `evict_scrub_batch_size` -> "128" and `scan_window_ms` -> "50".
deploy-bot: deploy started: revert-evict-scrub-config to canary cluster.
julia: thanks. also we should add a perf test that exercises seqlen 4096+ tails in CI perf job so this doesn't regress again.
ci-bot: raised an issue: perf-suite enhancement: add longtail soak matrix (seqlen 2048/4096, concurrency 16/32).
dylan: once canary stable for 15m we can decide whether to roll out config revert cluster-wide or prepare a full PR revert.
mark: logging followup: I'll log additional slab histograms and enable `evict_trace` on a few hosts to capture eviction latencies.
priya: note for postmortem: root cause = scrub v2 changes increased mark activity and deferred compaction -> increased fragmentation + slower free rate, exacerbated by kernel-router v2 allocation ordering.
julia: good summary. for now watch canary and set alert threshold lower (memory per-pod +10%) so we get earlier alarms. :eyes:
mark: will do. thanks team.
priya: if canary OOMs stop after config revert we can close this as config rollout issue, else escalate to revert PR.
julia: updating on-call and adding to incidents if it spikes again.
mark: +1.
